official_measurement_examples.name: Legal contaminated-land definition
official_measurement_examples.fact: Part 2A is risk based: the presence of contaminants or a historic industrial use alone does not make land legally contaminated land; unacceptable risk must be established under the statutory framework.

official_measurement_examples.name: Planning system role
official_measurement_examples.fact: Government planning guidance says most redevelopment-related contamination can be addressed through the planning system, while Part 2A is a separate statutory regime used where appropriate.

official_measurement_examples.name: LCRM staged process
official_measurement_examples.fact: LCRM separates Stage 1 risk assessment, Stage 2 options appraisal and Stage 3 remediation/verification; completing one stage does not prove the later stages have succeeded.

official_measurement_examples.name: Conceptual site model
official_measurement_examples.fact: LCRM Stage 1 requires potential contaminant linkages and a conceptual site model; a historic-use polygon or desk-study flag is only screening evidence.

official_measurement_examples.name: Verification requirement
official_measurement_examples.fact: LCRM Stage 3 requires evidence that remediation objectives and criteria have been met and a verification report; remediation intent or planning condition discharge cannot be presumed from a proposal alone.

official_measurement_examples.name: 2026 voluntary advice scope
official_measurement_examples.fact: The Environment Agency service published 3 June 2026 is restricted to contamination affecting controlled waters and outside specified planning/discharge-condition consultation contexts.

official_measurement_examples.name: Site condition report distinction
official_measurement_examples.fact: An H5 site condition report records land and groundwater condition for environmental permitting; it is not a Part 2A determination or planning permission.

official_measurement_examples.name: Planning permission limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Planning permission does not itself demonstrate contamination has been investigated, remediated and verified to the required standard; conditions and other regulatory controls may remain.

core_rules: historic industrial use is not a Part2A determination
contaminant presence alone is not unacceptable risk
planning contamination controls and Part2A must remain separate
LCRM Stage1 is not Stage2 or Stage3 completion
a desk-study flag is not a verified contaminant linkage
remediation strategy is not successful remediation verification
verification requires lines of evidence and a final record
planning permission is not contamination clearance
Part2A determination is not planning permission
H5 site condition report is an environmental-permit record not title or planning consent
voluntary remediation advice has a controlled-waters and process scope
radioactive contaminated land has a distinct statutory regime
contamination evidence does not determine ownership or development yield
absence of a national contamination flag is not proof of clean land
no parcel contamination clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
source_verification_note: Official Environment Agency, GOV.UK and legislation.gov.uk sources checked on 2026-07-26. The May-June 2026 technical collection and voluntary-remediation updates were retained with Part2A/planning/LCRM/H5 separation; no parcel clearance was promoted.
